verbalization: Woodfordin A is shown to interact with High affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1, which in turn is targeted by multiple compounds, including Isoglochidiolide, 16alpha-Hydroxymollic acid, and (4R)-3-methylidene-4-prop-1-en-2-ylcyclohexene. All these compounds have a final score of 0.5248 or higher, suggesting a plausible biological relationship. The shared target of Phosphodiesterase 6C across these compounds implies that the interaction may involve a mechanism that modulates the activity of this enzyme. The presence of multiple compounds with similar target profiles suggests a potential mechanism of action that could involve the regulation of cationic amino acid transport, which in turn may influence the activity of Phosphodiesterase 6C. The evidence supports a possible role for Woodfordin A in modulating the activity of Phosphodiesterase 6C through its interaction with the cationic amino acid transporter, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the exact mechanism.
